questions.question_text: Which list places the archive numbers $4\,306\,800$, $4\,360\,080$ and $4\,308\,600$ in ascending order?

options.why: Listed the numbers in descending order instead of the ascending order requested.

Began comparing at the thousands digit and skipped the ten-thousands place, so $4\,360\,080$ (thousands digit $0$) was ranked below $4\,306\,800$ (thousands digit $6$) and $4\,308\,600$ (thousands digit $8$).
Identified $4\,360\,080$ as the largest correctly, then ordered the other two by their last three digits and put $600$ before $800$ instead of comparing the thousands place.

questions.question_text: Which list orders the town populations $28\,056\,800$, $28\,506\,080$ and $28\,065\,008$ from smallest to largest?

options.why: Listed the populations from greatest to least instead of smallest to largest.
Skipped the hundred-thousands place and ordered by the ten-thousands digits $0$, $5$ and $6$.
Correctly placed the largest population last, but compared the final groups $008$ and $800$ before the thousands groups of the other two.
Compared the ones group $700$ with $770$ before checking the higher thousands group.
Treated the same non-zero digits as equal even though the zeros place them in different columns.
Assumed a comparison cannot be made despite both complete whole numbers being given.

questions.solution_text:
The first difference is in the ten-thousands place: $9>0$.
$103\,009\,770$ is smaller.

questions.question_text:
Attendances are $9\,870\,300$, $9\,807\,030$, $9\,873\,000$ and $9\,870\,030$.
Which attendance is greatest?

options.why: Compared only the final three digits and chose $300$ over $030$ and $000$, ignoring the thousands groups.
Compared only the last two digits, chose $30$ over $00$, and used the larger thousands group to break the tie.
Skipped the ten-thousands place and selected the largest thousands digit, $7$.

questions.solution_text:
The thousands groups are $870$, $807$, $873$ and $870$.
$873$ is greatest, so the greatest attendance is $9\,873\,000$.

options.why: Skipped the ten-thousands place and compared the thousands digits $9$ and $0$.
Compared only the matching millions and final groups, ignoring the different thousands groups.
Assumed that matching leading digits prevent a comparison, although all remaining digits are given.

questions.solution_text:
The first difference is in the ten-thousands place: $0<9$.
$66\,590\,080$ is greater.

options.why: Reversed the comparison of the thousands groups $010$ and $099$, placing $099$ before $010$ in ascending order.
Correctly placed the smallest value first, then listed the remaining values from greatest to least instead of least to greatest.
Ordered all four values from greatest to least instead of least to greatest.

questions.question_text:
An integer is greater than $45\,607\,997$ and less than $45\,608\,002$.
Which list gives all the possible integers in ascending order?

options.why: Included both bounds even though the integer must be strictly greater than the lower bound and strictly less than the upper bound.
Skipped $45\,608\,000$ when crossing into the next thousand.
Listed the valid integers in descending order instead of ascending order.

questions.solution_text:
Exclude both bounds and list every integer between them.
$45\,607\,998 < 45\,607\,999 < 45\,608\,000 < 45\,608\,001$

questions.question_text:
Connie lists her scores: $15\,098$, $14\,456$, $15\,724$, $15\,402$.
Which list shows the scores from smallest to largest?

options.why: Ordered by the final three digits $098$, $402$, $456$ and $724$, ignoring the thousands groups.
Correctly placed the smallest score first, then ordered the remaining scores by their last two digits $02$, $24$ and $98$.
Listed the scores from greatest to least instead of smallest to largest.

questions.solution_text:
The $14$-thousand score is smallest. Within the $15$-thousand scores, $098<402<724$.
$14\,456 < 15\,098 < 15\,402 < 15\,724$
